direction: D13: Proposal quality and the proposer prompt (critic pass)
refuted_claims:
1. Claim: "Code joins them as 'When <when>: <do>. Otherwise, <otherwise>.', which guarantees the form and the 600-character limit." Checked: the arithmetic of the stated slot limits with the join string in check.py. Found: 200 + 300 + 120 characters plus the 21 fixed join characters gives 641, which is over 600. The guarantee needs slot limits that sum to 579 or less, or a separate check of the joined text. check.py already had that separate check, and the pilot's D2 rule hit it at 917 and then 709 characters.

2. Claim: the declared opposite-code pairs (SearchQA D1/D2, D4/D5; OfficeQA D2/D3, D1/D5; LiveMath D1/D2, D3/D4; SpreadsheetBench D3/D4, D2/D6; ALFWorld D3/D4, D1/D2). The v5 prompt tells the proposer that these failures mean "the solver erred in the other direction". Checked against protocol.TAXONOMY. Found: only 3 of the 10 pairs are opposites:
   - SearchQA D1 (extra words) vs D2 (part missing or another form);
   - LiveMath D1 (missed the meta option) vs D2 (wrongly chose it);
   - LiveMath D3 (weaker option) vs D4 (stronger option).
   The other 7 pair different error types:
   - SearchQA D4 (wrong candidate) vs D5 (wrong kind);
   - OfficeQA D2 (wrong method) vs D3 (calculation slip), and D1 (wrong data) vs D5 (not in the document);
   - SpreadsheetBench D3 (hardcoded) vs D4 (wrong logic). v3's own E-ds s4-r4 targeted D3 and D4 in one rule. Also D2 vs D6;
   - ALFWorld D3 (search loop) vs D4 (invalid actions), and D1 (wrong object) vs D2 (missing step).
   The only pair the pilot tested (SearchQA D1/D2) is one of the 3 real ones.

3. Claim: "Within-reply pairs appear in 5 of 10 replies, each pair built on opposite-direction taxonomy codes". Checked: the codes in proposals_traced. Found: this holds for 3 of 5 pairs: I-ds s1 (D1/D2), E-ds s1 (D1/D2), and I-ds s3, where D4 faces an invalid row whose text is about weaker options (D3). It does not hold for E-ds s3 (D1 meta option vs D4) or E-ds s4 (D3+D4 vs D1+D5).

4. Claim: "prepare-stage survival rises from 28 of 49 to about 37-40 of 49". Checked: the would-be code-based triggers of the 9 mechanically voided rules, recomputed from the train units and diagnoses. Found:
   - The explorer's own accounting (28 + 8 evidence-invalid + 1 invalid row + 0-2 leaks) tops out at 39.
   - E-ds s2-r5 (D5) would have had a trigger of 2, below MIN_TRIGGER 4, so the range is 36-38.
   - More survivors are not a gain under the proposed cap of 5 per stage; they become extra selftest and screen arms. In v3, each screened rule arm cost 0.55-1.7M solver tokens on the QA and spreadsheet stages and 10.8M on ALFWorld (69.6M for the 15 screened arms).

5. Claims about the best pilot rule: "covers all 5 D1", "3 of 72 exposed", "harm exposure 3 of 72 vs 72 of 72 for a global rule", and "upper bound 5 items". Checked: applied the rule's literal action (delete answer words that also occur in the question) to the run-0 final answers on its 14 check-half items, against the references. Found:
   - It fixes 2 of the 5 D1 failures (Sirius Satellite Radio -> Sirius; Chester A. Arthur -> Arthur).
   - On 2 others the reference itself contains the deleted word: "the University of Wisconsin", and "George Bush", where deletion leaves "H. W.". One more is a plural mismatch (giblet vs Giblets).
   - It fixes 0 of the 6 non-D1 failures.
   - It turns all 3 exposed always-correct answers wrong: "bubble gum" -> "bubble", "Salt Lake City" -> "Salt Lake", "The Polar Express" -> "The Polar".
   - So the upper bound is 2, not 5, and literal application nets +2 / -3.
   - The judge-sized trigger (11 items, at most 2 fixable = 18%) dilutes the panel rather than raising it above v3's ~29%. The code-based D1 trigger would have 2 fixable of 5-6.
   - "72 of 72" is not a measured harm: in cal-1, the global rule cand moved 44 items down and 37 up out of 200.
   - Judge applicability is not what the solver does, because the rule text is shown on every item.

6. Claim: "the 3 wasted re-asks ... disappear". Found in the pilot: 1 of 4 v5 calls needed a re-ask (v3: 3 of 13). The re-ask re-sent the full 74 KB payload (22,319 tokens against 23,857 for the first call) and still broke 3 limits (709 > 600 characters). The waste recurred at the same rate.

7. Claim: "explicit constraints, checked by code: not already said". Found: this cannot be checked by code. The explorer's own word-overlap proxy failed to separate restatements from new advice (0.21 vs 0.18); code can only check that "covered" is a verbatim quote. In the pilot all 7 rules answered covered "none", because the parent was the empty E-ds scaffold.

8. Claim on cost: "11-16 calls x 25-45k = 0.3-0.7M per chain; total 1-2M GLM tokens per chain, under 2% of 139M". Found:
   - This counts one sample per code, but the recommendation is 2 samples, which doubles it.
   - OfficeQA per-code calls would sit at the 220 KB input cap; v3's OfficeQA analyst calls cost 80-82k tokens each, not 25-45k.
   - The recommended 3-vote judging triples the 31k judge pass.
   - The solver cost of the extra screened arms (point 4) is left out.
   - Likely 1.5-3M GLM tokens per chain before any solver cost.

9. verdict_cn says 3 whole replies were re-asked because one field was 4-21 characters over a limit. Found: 2 replies failed on transfer.none at 307 and 321 characters (7 and 21 over 300). The third (I-ds s5) failed because all 5 rows lacked placement. The 4-character overage (adds 304) was a single row (I-ds s3-r3), not a whole-reply rejection.

10. "7 of 7 conditional" is conditional in form only, forced by the template. Only 2 of the 7 (a-r3, b-r1) pass all of the design's own checks (limits, share below 0.5, judge-based MIN_TRIGGER):
   - a-r1 holds on 49 of 97 items, so it is global by the v5.1 rule;
   - a-r2 and the D2 rule break limits;
   - b-r2 (0) and b-r3 (3) fail the judge-based trigger.
missing:
1. Good-instruction baseline. The pilot ran on E-ds, whose parent is the empty scaffold. The I-ds seed was not in the payload, so neither restating the good instruction nor contradicting it could be detected. b-r1 ("delete words the question supplies") is in tension with the seed bullet "Prefer an answer that appears verbatim in the snippets ... keeping the source's wording avoids risk", and the D2 rule paraphrases seed bullets 4-5. An I-ds s1 pilot is needed before claiming v5 avoids restatement.

2. Transfer to similar benchmarks (the owner's metric). Placement and transfer are removed from the proposer with no replacement step. Per-code conditions pushed below a 0.3 share are bench-specific by construction, which likely lowers applicability on similar benchmarks. Not discussed.

3. The completed cal-1 (analysis.json, available before the explorer ran) answers the "cand vs seed-rule" head-on test. By its numbers (rule-arm per-item sd 0.25-0.33, so roughly ±0.11-0.15 or 2-3 items at n=20), the proposed ~1.6M-token 6-arm, 20-item screen pilot cannot resolve a ≤2-item effect.

4. Prior art not cited:
   - AutoGuide (Fu et al., NeurIPS 2024; https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/d8efbb5dd415974eb095c3f06bff1f48-Abstract.html, https://arxiv.org/html/2403.08978v2): conditional "When <context> ..." guidelines mined from contrastive success/failure trajectory pairs and selected at test time by context (k=2). ALFWorld 79.1% vs ExpeL 59.0%. Its WebShop ablation (guidelines without contexts 37% vs full 46%) points to the selection step; no error bars are reported.
   - UniPrompt / Task Facet Learning (Findings ACL 2025; https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10504): per-cluster minibatches, because random-batch feedback did not generalize. This supports per-code calls.
   - ACE (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.04618): grow-and-refine curation, relevant to the merge-time consistency check.
   AutoGuide implies the missing design option: evaluate the condition at solve time and show the rule only when it holds. That would make "harm exposure" real; v5 keeps the rule as text that is always on.

5. Conditions that code can check (b-r1 is plain word overlap, 97/97) need no GLM judge. Prefer such conditions (links to D4).

6. Judge-sized triggers should be intersected with the target code. Otherwise they fill with failures the rule cannot fix (b-r1: 6 of 11).

7. Overlap with v4: context §4 already lists per-code calls with balanced evidence, the conditional template, judge-sized triggers, the re-ask with errors and 3-vote judging as v4 work. The genuinely new v5 content is small: slot join, transfer removal, 2 samples per code, share estimate, conditions on the draft, cross-code check.

8. Four of the five benchmarks were not piloted. OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld conditions need page, workbook or episode context, and the judge cost there is a guess.

9. A cheaper re-ask is not specified: send only the failing row and its errors (about 1-2k tokens) instead of the full payload.

notes_cn: 核查：多数数字在原始数据上重算后对得上（49条规则的去向、3次整份重问浪费约18.7万计费单位、新写法需27次调用）。但几处说过头：①“最好的规则”只是条件命中全部5道目标错题，照字面执行只能改对2道，还会把碰到的3道做对题改错；②方案定的“反方向错误”配对，按错误分类定义，10对里只有3对真是反方向；③三栏上限相加最多641字，保证不了600字上限；④试验从空白起点做，没放入好的任务说明，检验不了“不重复好说明”；⑤成本少算了每类问两次、评判投票三次和后续多测规则的花费；⑥已完成的校准实验显示单条规则效果约为零，计划中的20题小试验测不出差别。
